general.description: Master Services Agreements (routine and complex), SaaS addenda, AI Platform Agreements, R&D and clinical-trial modules (GXP, CT Conduct, Purchase Orders), SharePoint templates, “battle of the forms”, suite of contract documents, academic vs commercial distinctions
Definition of services and deliverables, service-level metrics and credits, project plans, performance expectations, supplier negotiation guidance
Charges and payment terms, change-order process, Incoterms, pricing amendments, purchase-order mechanics
Limitations of liability, warranties and representations, insurance requirements, indemnification provisions including AI-specific nuances
Intellectual-property rights and ownership across MSA, SaaS, AI, and R&D arrangements; publication and records clauses
Confidentiality agreements and clauses, confidentiality of negotiating positions, GDPR/data-privacy obligations, data-processing terms
Data-protection obligations, cybersecurity requirements, disaster-recovery and business-continuity planning, technical security standards
Compliance with laws and sanctions, GxP (GDP/GLP/GMP) applications, trade controls, third-party sustainability expectations, adverse-event reporting
Subcontracting, assignment and novation, parties and affiliates, roles and responsibilities tables, principal-investigator designation, expectations of third parties
Term and termination, consequences of termination, force-majeure events, governing law and jurisdiction, dispute-resolution clauses, audit rights and records

privacy.description: EU, UK and Swiss Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), PRC cross-border contracts, UK International Data-Transfer Addendum, transfer safeguards, description of data transferred
GDPR, UK Data-Protection Act, Swiss Data-Protection Law, PRC PIPL, impact of local laws on contract performance
Controller-processor distinctions, Data-Protection Appendix structure and purpose, supplier and overseas-recipient obligations, definitions of personal-information handling
Encryption, access controls, physical security, incident-management procedures and other technical and organisational safeguards
Processes for handling data-subject requests, duration of processing, data erasure or return, description of personal information provided abroad
Sub-processor approval requirements, flow-down obligations, supplier oversight and documentation
Personal-data-breach notification duties, incident-response procedures, obligations in case of public-authority access
Audit rights, compliance demonstration, record-keeping requirements, attachments and documentation of processing activities
Liability caps, indemnification, remedies for breach, non-compliance termination provisions
Competent supervisory authorities, governing-law clauses, jurisdiction selection, local-law carve-outs
Roles and obligations of controllers, processors, and sub-processors including data-handling duties, mutual responsibilities, and regulatory alignment

alexion.description: Service Agreements for single, defined engagements; Master Service Agreements (MSAs) when repeat work with the same vendor is likely; Statements of Work (SOWs) that outline deliverables and timelines under an MSA; Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) whenever personal data is handled.

Purchase Orders (POs) with standard T&Cs for spends below $10 k; Alexion contract templates and legal review required above $10 k; additional thresholds for healthcare-professional or high-value services; Request-for-Proposal (RFP) workflow for complex projects.
Use of the iCertis platform to create agreements, route them through approval and legal review stages, track lifecycle status, and resubmit drafts after comments until ready for signature.
Mandatory 3PRM assessments before onboarding, vendor-master requests via AskAZ, monitoring of financial and compliance risk, plus supplier-diversity and sustainability initiatives.

Country-specific maximum payment terms, milestone-based payments tied to approved deliverables, procedures for handling late payments, and capped pass-through or management fees to prevent budget overruns.
Category structure covering Global Operations, IT & Telecom, Marketing & Market Access, Medical Affairs, Professional Services, and R&D; with named category leads and regional sourcing contacts.

DPAs for data protection, Pharmacovigilance language when patient or HCP data is involved, Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements (CDAs) for early discussions, and adherence to GMP/GCP, GDPR and other local legal standards.
